title: Hardcoded Deployment-Dependent Resource and Connection Settings
pattern: Source constants fix resource capacities or volatile deployment settings (cache/buffer/pool sizes, timeouts, service IPs, ports, URLs, credentials) that need to vary with resource limits or environment, instead of deriving them at startup or reading them from external configuration.
why_bad: The binary can over-allocate and OOM on a smaller host or waste resources on a larger one, and operators cannot adapt it to a new environment (sandbox, staging, production) or mitigate an incident such as shrinking a pool during an outage without a full build, compile, and redeploy cycle.
detection: Compiled cache, buffer, or pool capacities that ignore effective host/container limits; compile-time constants for connection pool sizing or socket timeouts that cannot be adjusted without a build; or hardcoded IP addresses, URLs, ports, or other environmental parameters in constants, socket-connection string literals, or client constructors/structs with no configuration or discovery override.
source: Gregg, Brendan - *Systems Performance_ Enterprise and the Cloud* (2013, Pearson Education Limited (US titles)_Prentice Hall).pdf, Chapter 7; Titus Winters, Tom Manshreck, Hyrum Wright - *Software Engineering at Google_ Lessons Learned from Programming Over Time* (2020, O'Reilly Media).pdf, Chapter 23.; *Release It!*, "Configuration," p. 251.; Andrew Hunt, David Thomas, *The Pragmatic Programmer* (2019), Topic 32, "Configuration", p. 581-582.
